scope: Catalog the 60 game-logic call sites of [[Engine_AsyncActorEvent_Producer_Wrapper_FUN_007CE7B0]]. Extract the opcode each producer fires and infer the receiving Element subclass via the element-vtable8-bulk pass's slot-8 case sets. Closes the Pattern B async event bus producer-to-consumer mapping.

method.step1: Listed 63 callers of FUN_007CE7B0 (one of the producer wrappers; the second wrapper FUN_007CE780 has 2 callers already in the main set, so 64 unique callers; one VA in the batch missed Ghidra's function boundary so 63 parsed).
method.step2: Bulk-decomped all 63 callers via DumpFunctionDecomp.java -> 6864-line decomp file producer_callers.txt.
method.step3: Parsed the decomp programmatically (parse_producers.py) - extract FUN_007ce7b0(<opcode>, ...) call lines and extract the literal opcode constant. 80 call sites total, 78 with literal opcodes, 2 with variable opcodes.
method.step4: Cross-referenced opcodes against the element-vtable8-bulk pass's per-class slot-8 case sets (8 Element subclasses with per-class dispatchers). 39 of 46 distinct opcodes mapped cleanly to exactly one Element class. 2 opcodes (0x09, 0x0A) ambiguous between CutManagerElement and EffectElement (overlap). 7 opcodes (0x1B..0x21) unmatched - all from one broadcaster producer FUN_006125E0.
method.step5: Identified 60 callers-with-calls, 4 multi-opcode producers (FUN_00662440 fires 0x5B+0x5C, FUN_006195D0 fires 0x13+0x2E, FUN_008A84C0 fires 0xA+0xB, FUN_006125E0 broadcasts 0x19..0x23 - 11 opcodes total).

key_findings: 60 distinct producer functions across the FUN_006XXXXX..FUN_008XXXXX game-logic range fire async events on Element actors via the Pattern B queue.

Producer-to-class clustering aligns with code-section subsystem boundaries: FUN_0061XXXX cluster -> CutManagerElement (cutscene system); FUN_0061[8-B]XXX -> CameraElement; FUN_006[2-6]XXXX -> MapLayoutElement; FUN_0066XXXX -> CharaElement; FUN_008XXXXX -> Cut/Effect mix.
78 of 80 call sites pass a literal opcode constant. The remaining 2 are variable-driven (FUN_007ce7b0(uVar3, ...) - opcode chosen at runtime).

**FUN_006125E0 is an init/reset broadcaster** - fires 11 sequential opcodes 0x19..0x23 in one function. This explains why the 0x1B..0x21 range appears unmatched: they are fired but not handled by any cataloged Element slot-8. Hypothesis: either an Element class was missed in the element-vtable8-bulk pass's RTTI enumeration (e.g., Application::Main::SqwtInterface::CustomControl::LogElement/TileElement which were excluded from the namespace filter), or these are extra-broadcast opcodes with no current consumer (forward-compat with future Element subclasses).

CharaElement opcode 0x59 has 3 producers (most of any opcode) - all 3 originate in different code regions (FUN_00611c30 also fires 0x06, FUN_0061b5a0 also fires 0x13). Suggests 0x59 is a frequently-triggered CharaElement event (probably actor state-change broadcast).
0x13 / 0x2E (CameraElement) have 4 / 1 producers respectively. 0x13 is the dominant camera event.

Async event bus serves at minimum 7 of the 8 Element classes catalogued by the element-vtable8-bulk pass (BootupElement and LightElement have empty slot-8 bodies and no observed producers in this scan).

The 2 variable-opcode call sites are interesting - they suggest a 'forward-this-opcode' pattern where the producer dispatches whatever opcode was given to it (router/proxy pattern). Worth follow-up but low priority.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: AsyncEvent_Broadcaster_FUN_006125E0
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: Pattern B async event bus broadcaster - fires 11 sequential opcodes (0x19..0x23) via FUN_007CE7B0. Likely init/reset path that signals to GameManagerElement (0x19,0x1A), an uncataloged Element class (0x1B..0x21), and MapLayoutElement (0x22,0x23). This is the function that surfaces the 7-opcode gap in the element-vtable8-bulk pass's slot-8 catalog.
